learning_outcomes.text: Master the main methods for the functional analysis of machines and mechanisms.
Knowledge of the main mechanisms and motion transmission systems, with reference to examples of energy conversion machines and friction and wear phenomena.
Acquire the basic knowledge of dynamics and vibrations necessary to describe the dynamic behavior of a mechanical system with particular reference to machines for energy production.
Provide the ability to study mechanical vibrations, their causes and the effects they produce.

syllabus_topics: Definition of machine and classification into operating and generating machines.
Kinematic pairs and mechanisms: analytical and graphical tools for kinematic and kinetostatic study of mechanisms.
Examples of mechanisms for moving energy production systems.
Friction and wear in machines and mechanisms.
Examples of evaluating mechanical efficiency in energy production machines.
Gears and mechanisms for motion transmission.
Examples of motion transmission with gears in energy production machines, used in wind turbines, hydraulic turbines and internal combustion engines.
Examples of lumped parameter modeling of energy production machines.
Definitions of machine, kinematic chain, mechanism.
Wear, Reye's hypothesis and contact pressure distribution.
Kinematic analysis of the slider-crank mechanism and four-bar linkage.
Joints: universal joint and homokinetic joints.
Kinematic and kinetostatic analysis of mechanisms and kinetostatics of vehicles.
Efficiency of machines in series and in parallel and examples.
Definition of conjugate profiles and tracing methods.
Cylindrical involute gears. Geometric characteristics and normal dimensioning. Conditions for continuity of motion and non-interference. Helical cylindrical gears. Conical gears.
Mechanical systems with flexible elements: belt drives.
Underdamped, overdamped and critically damped response.
Forced vibrations. Transient solution. Analytical solution. Amplitude and phase with damping. Resonances.
Base isolation: Analytical solution and suspension optimization.
Mass isolation: Analytical solution, suspension optimization
Free vibrations of a linear viscous system with multiple degrees of freedom.
Orthogonality properties of natural modes of vibration.
Exercises in kinematics, motion transmission, vibration isolation.

assessment_methods.method: Discussion of a paper on dynamic modeling and transmission design of an energy production machine

assessment_rules: The assessment includes a written exam, an oral exam, and the discussion of a paper on dynamic modeling and transmission design of an energy production machine. There is a possibility of intermediate exemptions during the course.
